chunks: And by this chain, from Al-Washsha', from 'Alī ibn Al-Ḥasan, from Abān ibn Taghlib, who said:

Abū 'Abdillāh (عليه السلام) said: “How will you be when the violent seizure occurs between the two masjids, and knowledge withdraws just as the snake withdraws into its hole, and the Shī'ah differ, and some of them call others liars, and some of them spit in the faces of others?”
I said: “May I be sacrificed for you, there is no good in that.” So he said to me: “All good is at that time,” three times.

key_terms.الشِّيعَةُ: the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt who become divided in this trial
key_terms.الْبَطْشَةُ: a forceful seizure or violent strike occurring in a time of trial
key_terms.الْحَيَّةُ: the snake, used here in a simile for retreat and concealment
key_terms.الْخَيْرُ: the good that Imam al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام) says is entirely present in that time
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: religious knowledge that becomes withdrawn or concealed
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَيْنِ: the two masjids, referring to a known sacred setting in the report
key_terms.جُحْرِهَا: its hole, the place into which the snake retreats
key_terms.كَذَّابِينَ: liars, an accusation exchanged between opposing groups

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام) say about the time when knowledge withdraws and the Shī'ah become divided?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a time of severe trial marked by conflict, concealment of knowledge, and division among the Shī'ah. Despite the apparent corruption and social breakdown, Imam al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام) emphasizes that all good will be in that period, indicating a hidden divine wisdom within the tribulation.

en.hubeali: And by this chain, from Al Washa’a, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Aban Bin Taghlub who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How would you be when the seizure occurs between the two Masjids, so the knowledge would be obscured just as the obscurity of the snake into its hole, and the Shias would differ, and some of them would be calling the others to be liars, and some of them would be spitting in the faces of others’.
I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! There would not be any goodness during that’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The goodness, all of it, would be during that’ – three (times)’.
en.sarwar: 17. through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from al-Washsha’ from Ali ibn al-Hassan from Aban ibn Taghlib who has said the following.

“How would it be with you when an lagre scale attack would take place between the two mosques. Thereafter, knowledge will become obscure as the snake goes in to its hiding place. The Shi‘a (Muslims) will hold differences and one group will call the group liars and one group will spit onto the faces of the aother.”
I then said, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, there will be nothing good in such conditions.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “All goodness will be there.” He said it three times.
